result:
Implemented Alternative B: the grade report attached to a notification no longer carries a QR code and is no longer stored.

I did not run the tests, and I did not reproduce the failure before changing anything.

I did not confirm the exact symptom. From reading the code, the attachment goes through the same QR-code path as a student's own download. That path draws the QR code and, in `new_document` (`app/helpers/pdf_helper.rb`), creates a stored `Report` record and file for every PDF. That is what the issue describes as storing hundreds of reports at once.

- **`app/helpers/pdf_helper.rb`:** `setup_pdf_config` accepts a `no_qr_code` option. When the active configuration uses a QR code, it switches to no signature, so no QR code is drawn and no `Report` or file is created.
- **`app/controllers/concerns/shared_pdf_concern.rb`:** `render_enrollments_grades_report_pdf` takes a `no_qr_code:` keyword and passes it to the view.
- **`app/views/enrollments/grades_report_pdf.pdf.prawn`:** it forwards `no_qr_code`, and also turns on the existing watermark so the document is visibly not official. I reused the existing watermark text rather than writing a new one, so the exact wording of the "conference only" notice is still open.
- **`app/controllers/notifications_controller.rb`:** `prepare_attachments` now requests the report with `no_qr_code: true`.

The student's own grade report download and the other PDFs are unchanged. Each notification recipient still gets their own report, because the attachment is generated per enrollment.
